evidence.clarity: H1 'Every licensed kitchen has hours it sits empty.' is an observation, not the product; the lede ('Ovenhour rents them out. A kitchen lists the hours it's closed... A small food maker books a shift') makes it clear, and the two hero buttons name each audience ('I make food and need a kitchen' / 'I run a kitchen with empty hours'). The kitchen button does not say what happens (it leaves for ovenhour.example/kitchens sign-up).
evidence.fit: Both sides get a real path: amber maker button scrolls to a waiting-list panel, kitchen button goes to the supplied ovenhour.example/kitchens. County uncertainty gets its own section ('Ovenhour hasn't announced launch counties yet... we won't guess on your behalf') and a 'Where Ovenhour is today' status grid (Listings: None yet). The shared listing with 'If you run the kitchen' and 'If you're the maker' margins resolves the two-websites tension well. Undercut by a maker form that promises 'we'll email you when a kitchen within reach lists its hours' with no backend to do it.
evidence.distinctiveness: The dark 'hour board' (bakery / dinner restaurant / caterer rows with hatched busy blocks and amber empty blocks, '14 empty hours') is a product-born motif, and the 'One shift, by the clock' kitchen/maker table is specific. Structure is still section-head + intro grid repeated four times, and the serif display falls back to a Times-like face in Chromium on Linux, which reads closer to default than intended.
evidence.proof: The hour board sits just below the hero (peeks in at y~830 at 1440) but is a static illustration of the problem, not the product. The actual product artifact, the sample listing ('Weeknight shift, 10 pm to 5 am', equipment, house rules), starts around the third screen at 1440 and is static. Numbers are internally consistent (3+11=14, 14+1=15, 9+10=19) and labelled 'Typical patterns... not listings' and 'Sample - Not a real kitchen'.
evidence.craft: 1440 first screen: the headline/lede column occupies the left ~600px and the right half of the hero (roughly x 740-1300, y 150-700) is empty. 768: the board keeps its three-column row grid, so the track is ~270px and fitLabels hides 6 of 9 segment labels; the bakery row has no labels at all, and the axis crowds '6 pm' against '12 am'. probe axe reports one serious colour-contrast node at 390 and 1440. Elsewhere the spacing rhythm and listing card are tidy.
evidence.mobile: 390: board is recomposed well (name and count above a full-width track, labels such as 'Empty 1 pm - 3 am' fit), no overflow, CTAs 45px tall and stacked. But the nav is four plain links wrapping under the logo at 22px tall, the hour chips are 38px tall, and after an empty submit the error appears under the chips, below the fold relative to the Email field at the top of the form.
evidence.honesty: Examples are labelled where they appear (board footnote, 'Sample listing.' notice, 'Sample' tag, '$— per hour'). But the maker panel says 'Leave your details and we'll email you when a kitchen within reach lists its hours' and 'One email when there's something near you', and after submit at 390/1440 shows 'Noted. We'll email maria@market.example when a kitchen lists hours near Durham' while the only delivery is a mailto: the visitor has to send themselves; nothing says so before submit, and the hedge ('If that email doesn't go through on its own...') only appears after.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: hero buttons work (#makers anchor, external kitchens URL); chips toggle; empty submit shows 'We need an email address we can reach and the city and county you cook in.' but focus lands on City and county instead of Email (the indexOf('email') check fails because the message starts with 'an'); invalid email message works; valid submit hides the form and shows the confirmation in place. The board and listing have no controls. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and written: 'List the hours you're closed, not the hours you'd like to be paid for. A maker will turn up at the start of them.', 'If a piece of equipment isn't listed, it isn't yours for the night.', the county list (cottage-food registration, food-handler card). Button 'Email me when a kitchen lists' is clear but promises something that will not happen. Some repetition across board, listing, clock and county sections makes the page long.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede and two buttons, with the right half empty and the board's first row just entering at the bottom; the headline states a fact about kitchens rather than a promise. 390: headline, lede and both buttons fit, with the bakery row peeking at the bottom. Specific enough via the lede, but nothing operable or product-shaped is in view, and the maker action leads to a notification promise the product cannot keep.

problems: Maker waiting list reports success ('Noted. We'll email you when a kitchen lists...') while nothing is stored; the form only fires a mailto, and this is not stated before submit
Product artifact (sample listing) is static and arrives around the third screen; the hero at 1440 has a large empty right half
Hour board loses most of its labels at 768 (bakery row unlabelled, axis crowded), and form error focus goes to the wrong field

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The most prominent first-screen action at 1440 is the amber 'I make food and need a kitchen', which leads to the maker form whose submit 'Email me when a kitchen lists' is that action's completion. Copy before submit says 'Leave your details and we'll email you when a kitchen within reach lists its hours' and 'One email when there's something near you. Nothing else.' After submit the page shows 'Noted. We'll email <address> when a kitchen lists hours near <place>.' No data is stored or sent; script only sets window.location to a mailto: makers@ovenhour.example (an address the brief did not supply) that the visitor must send themselves. The page reports a sign-up that did not happen, without saying so before the visitor acted.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P001/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click 'I make food and need a kitchen'. Enter maria@market.example in Email and 'Durham' in City and county, click 'Email me when a kitchen lists'. Observe the 'Noted. We'll email maria@market.example when a kitchen lists hours near Durham' confirmation; inspect the inline script (maker-form submit handler): it only builds a mailto: href and sets window.location.href; no request or storage occurs.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Kitchens close at ten. Licenses don't.' is a slogan on its own, but the subhead says it plainly ('a booking site where licensed commercial kitchens rent their empty hours to small food makers'), and each button has a line saying what happens ('Sign-up is open now. No maker can book yet...', 'No account. Your note goes to the founders' inbox with your county on it.').
evidence.fit: The 'Read as the kitchen / a maker' toggle on one example sheet is a deliberate answer to 'both sides without two websites': the same sheet relabels its fields (Makers may use -> You get, House rules -> You agree to). Kitchens go to the supplied URL; makers get a note form that states 'It opens as an email to the founders; nothing is stored here.' County uncertainty is handled ('We have not chosen launch counties'). Kitchen action is visually primary although makers are the louder side; defensible since only kitchens can sign up.
evidence.distinctiveness: Mono time-axis roster with amber listed blocks, grey service and dashed 'held' blocks, 'EXAMPLE LISTING' stamp, and step fragments ('fryer: off limits', 'Thu 22:00-06:00 · 8 h') reuse the sheet's vocabulary. Recognisable without the logo. The 1-2-3 'how it works' band and closing CTA band are familiar structure.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the sheet's header, toggle and Mon-Wed rows are in the first viewport (sheet top 501). It responds: holding Tue drops the panel to '8 blocks · 68 h'; in maker mode, selecting Sun shows 'Sun 18:00-06:00 · 12 h' and '12 h × $38 = $456 at the illustrative price'. Numbers are consistent (24+5×8+12=76 h) and labelled 'the hours, equipment and price are illustrative'. Small inconsistency: the service block tooltip reads 'Dinner service 09:00-21:30'.
evidence.craft: Clear type system (Helvetica bold display, mono for data labels), spacing tokens, crisp segmented toggle, white sheet on grey ground with consistent rules; no overflow and no axe violations at 390/1440. Minor: listed blocks are only 30px tall, the 1440 hero's bottom alignment leaves the space above the headline empty, and the legend wraps awkwardly at 390.
evidence.mobile: 390: real Menu button (44px) opens a stacked nav and closes after tapping 'County rules'; CTAs are 48px, full width, with their consequence lines; the sheet is reordered ahead of the side notes and its 'EXAMPLE LISTING' stamp is visible next to it. But the sheet starts at y~690, so its roster is on the second screen, blocks are 30px tall, and after tapping the Sun block the result panel (top ~893) is below the fold.
evidence.honesty: Every example is labelled where it appears ('EXAMPLE LISTING', 'illustrative: $38', 'No kitchen is listed yet'). Both actions say what happens before the click. Pricing band says Ovenhour's fee 'is not decided'. After maker submit at 390 it shows 'Opening your mail app with this note. If nothing opens, copy it to...' plus the composed note. Footer: 'Nothing on this page is a review, a booking count or a partner.'
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: mode toggle swaps labels and aria-pressed; kitchen-mode click holds a block (text becomes 'held', count and hint update); maker mode refuses held blocks (aria-disabled) and selects listed ones with a price line; Enter on a focused block works; switching back clears the selection. Menu toggles 'Menu'/'Close'. Empty form submit triggers native 'Please fill out this field.'; valid submit shows a copyable note. Hint says 'Click' on touch, and the result panel is off-screen after tapping a lower block at 390. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Tight, kitchen-world language: 'Mark the hours you are dark', 'The equipment list is the contract', 'Two ovens means two ovens.', 'Send the founders your shift'. Microcopy is written, not default. Small slips: 'Dinner service 09:00-21:30' tooltip, 'Click a block' on phones, and the H1 needs the subhead to land.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, plain subhead, two actions with their consequences, and the top of the operable example sheet with its label and toggle. 390: headline, subhead and both actions with consequence lines fit, but no artifact is in view (sheet begins at y~690 with only its stamp and title), so the promise is clear but not yet backed in the first phone screen.

problems: At 390 the shift sheet is on the second screen and, after tapping a block, the result panel lands below the fold
Listed blocks are 30px tall touch targets and the hint says 'Click'
H1 is a slogan that depends on the subhead; minor data slip in the 'Dinner service 09:00-21:30' tooltip

reason: B puts an operable, honestly labelled shift sheet in the first screen and lets the same sheet be read by kitchen or maker, which answers the brief's two-sides tension, and every action says what it does before the click. A has a strong editorial voice and a good hour-board motif, but its artifact is static and late, the hero wastes half the desktop viewport, and its maker form reports a sign-up that never happens. A would win only if its form disclosed the mailto up front and the sample listing became operable near the top.
